item.text: I’m checking the current source again to pick a refactor that changes structure, not just formatting. Given the codebase is still small, the useful move is likely to simplify the algorithm internals or make the test/demo layout more consistent.

I’m changing the partitioning strategy now. The current version is already correct, but a three-way partition removes a lot of unnecessary work on equal values and gives the implementation a cleaner structure around the “less / equal / greater” split.

I introduced the partition object, but the size calculation needs to live at the call site because it depends on the current range. I’m correcting that now and simplifying the helper so it only carries the partition boundaries.

I’m cleaning up the partition helper names while I fix the size logic. The goal is to make the partition boundaries read like the actual regions they represent, which avoids the off-by-one confusion that slipped in during the first draft.
The main algorithm refactor is in place. I’m compiling now to catch any naming or boundary mistakes before I touch the test harness.

I’m folding the tests into a table-driven layout next. The current file has the same structure repeated four times, so this is a straightforward quality win: fewer bespoke methods, clearer failure messages, and easier expansion if we add more edge cases.
I’m adding one more targeted test for the new three-way partition behavior. That gives the refactor a direct correctness check on the case it was meant to improve: lots of repeated values.
The structure work is done. I’m compiling and running the demo/tests again to verify that the three-way partition and the table-driven test harness both behave correctly.

Refactored the core quicksort implementation again in [QuickSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/010_quick_sort/QuickSort.java) and tightened the test harness in [QuickSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/010_quick_sort/QuickSortTest.java).

What changed:
- Switched partitioning to a three-way split (`< pivot`, `== pivot`, `> pivot`), which is cleaner and handles duplicate-heavy inputs better.
- Kept the half-open range convention throughout the implementation.
- Replaced the old partition-index recursion with explicit partition boundaries, which makes the control flow easier to follow.
- Simplified the tests into a table-driven `runCase(...)` style.
- Added a dedicated duplicate-heavy test to cover the new partition behavior.
- Aligned invalid-range expectations with `Objects.checkFromToIndex(...)`, which throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` for reversed bounds too.
